topic: How does the 45° scan range affect link budget calculations for edge-of-coverage users compared to broadside beams?
consensus_response: The 45° scan range significantly impacts link budget calculations for edge-of-coverage users compared to broadside beams.  This is due to the increased interference and weaker signal strengths experienced by these users.  While broadside beams offer stronger signals and precise beam control, leading to less conservative link budget calculations, the 45° scan range necessitates more conservative calculations to manage the weaker signals and increased interference. This results in lower power levels and smaller coverage areas for edge-of-coverage users.  The trade-off between signal strength and coverage area is crucial to consider when designing satellite communication systems.
